skill.name: app-store-changelog
skill.description: Generate clear App Store release notes from git history since the last tag or a specified ref.
skill.summary: Generates App Store release notes from user-visible git changes.
skill.author: Dimillian

security_audit.summary: Static command and reconnaissance matches were false positives in context: markdown inline code, local git metadata collection, and guidance to avoid internal details. I found one implementation weakness: the shell helper expands user-supplied git ranges without quoting, which can alter the git log query. No prompt injection, network access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unquoted git range expansion in the helper script
remediation.suggestion: Quote the computed range in both git log calls and validate user-provided refs with git rev-parse before use.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid internal codenames, ticket IDs, or file paths.
- Run `scripts/collect_release_changes.sh` from the repo root to gather commits and touched files.
- If needed, pass a specific tag or ref: `scripts/collect_release_changes.sh v1.2.3 HEAD`.
- `scripts/collect_release_changes.sh`: Collect commits and touched files since last tag.
- `references/release-notes-guidelines.md`: Language, filtering, and QA rules for App Store notes.
- Use clear verbs and plain language; avoid internal jargon.

semantic_findings.title: Unquoted Git Range Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The helper accepts optional git refs and expands the computed range without quotes in git log calls. A ref containing spaces or option-like content could alter the log query and expose more history than intended.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script takes refs from positional arguments and later expands the derived range unquoted in git log. This is a clear argument-splitting risk, though it is limited to local git commands.

content.value_statement: Release notes often mix technical commits with user-facing changes. This skill collects git history and turns visible changes into clear App Store copy.
actual_capabilities: Collects commits and touched files since the last git tag or a specified ref.
Converts technical commit history into user-facing App Store release notes.
Filters internal refactors, CI changes, dependencies, and developer-only work.
Groups visible changes by themes such as New, Improved, and Fixed.
Checks that each release-note bullet maps to a real change in the selected range.
limitations: Requires a local git repository with accessible history.
Does not verify app behavior, QA status, or shipped binaries.
May need human clarification for ambiguous commits or internal-only changes.
Does not publish releases or update App Store Connect metadata.

use_cases.title: Prepare iOS Release Notes
use_cases.description: Turn recent git commits into concise store update bullets before submitting an app update.

use_cases.title: Review User Impact
use_cases.description: Separate visible product changes from internal work before a release review meeting.

use_cases.title: Polish Storefront Copy
use_cases.description: Rewrite technical change summaries into plain language that users can understand quickly.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Latest Notes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for the default git range.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use app-store-changelog to create App Store release notes from the latest tag to HEAD.

prompt_templates.title: Use Custom Range
prompt_templates.scenario: Create notes for a known release branch or tag range.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate App Store update text for changes from v1.2.3 to HEAD. Group bullets by New, Improved, and Fixed.

prompt_templates.title: Filter Technical Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Remove internal changes before sharing with customers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the collected changes and omit internal refactors, CI updates, dependency changes, and file paths. Keep only user-visible changes.

prompt_templates.title: Produce Final Copy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release copy with a length constraint and verification step.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create final App Store release notes under 1,000 characters. Include only verified user-facing changes and flag any ambiguous commit separately.

output_examples.input: Generate release notes since the latest tag for a bug fix update.
output: Fixed media attachments not opening in full screen.
Improved timeline loading speed on slow connections.
Updated search results so recent items appear more reliably.

output_examples.input: Create App Store update copy from v2.4.0 to HEAD and remove internal changes.
output: Added faster account switching from the profile menu.
Improved upload progress messages for large files.
Fixed a sign-in issue that could block returning users.

output_examples.input: Summarize this release for App Store users in a shorter format.
output_examples.output: Added smoother account switching, improved uploads for large files, and fixed a sign-in issue for returning users.

best_practices: Run the skill from the repository root so git history and file paths resolve correctly.
Provide the exact tag or ref range when preparing notes for a specific release.
Review ambiguous commits with the product owner before finalizing storefront copy.
anti_patterns: Do not include internal ticket IDs, file paths, or implementation names in public notes.
Do not describe refactors, CI changes, or dependency updates as user-facing improvements.
Do not publish generated notes without checking that each bullet maps to a real shipped change.

faq.question: Does this skill publish to App Store Connect?
faq.answer: No. It drafts release-note text only. You must paste and publish the final copy yourself.

faq.question: Can I choose a specific release range?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a starting tag or ref and an optional ending ref, such as HEAD.

faq.question: What happens if the repository has no tags?
faq.answer: The helper script falls back to the available history for the selected ending ref.

faq.question: Will it include internal engineering changes?
faq.answer: It is designed to exclude refactors, CI work, dependency bumps, and other internal-only changes.

faq.question: Can it write notes for Android or web releases?
faq.answer: The guidance targets App Store copy, but the same workflow can help draft short user-facing release notes.

faq.question: Does it guarantee every change shipped in the app?
faq.answer: No. It reads git history and needs human review to confirm shipped behavior and release scope.
